items.t: 'A war of unmanned machines, AI and total transparency of the battlefield'

items.t: Putin says Ukraine hits Russian oil plants despite Trump’s requests, promises retaliation
items.m: MOSCOW, Nov 24 - Ukraine has continued attacks on Russian oil refineries despite requests from US President Donald Trump to refrain, Russian leader Vladimir Putin said on Tuesday, pledging to retaliate.

items.t: Ukrainian psyop radio mixes Russian rock with instructions on how to surrender, NYT reports
items.m: Ukraine’s Special Operations Forces run a network of radio transmitters that they use to wage psychological warfare against Russian troops, The New York Times reported. The transmitters air different programs tailored to conditions in each sector of the front line. The programs sound like local radio, except that the music and news alternate with instructions on how to surrender.

items.t: Hackers and media outlets expose what the Kremlin tried to hide: At least 500,000 dead on the Ukrainian front
items.m: Since Russian troops invaded Ukraine in February 2022, Vladimir Putin has blocked the publication of casualty figures. However, hackers have breached the records of Rosstat, the Russian federal statistics agency, and exiled media outlets have thoroughly examined the data. The death toll could exceed 700,000 if missing soldiers are included.

items.t: Belarus's Lukashenko proposes flying with Ukraine's Zelenskiy to Moscow for talks
items.m: Nov 24 - Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko, a close ally of Russian leader Vladimir Putin, proposed in an interview published on Tuesday that he and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy fly together to Moscow for Kremlin talks to end the war in Ukraine.

items.t: South Africa convicts Zimbabwean who tried to fight Ukraine for Russia
items.m: The Zimbabwean man was arrested on November 8 at a Johannesburg airport while attempting to board a flight to Russia.

items.t: U.K. warns of Russian sabotage threat to companies that supply Ukraine
items.m: The MI5 urged companies to take action to improve their security in the face of what they said was the risk posed by operatives acting for Russia.

items.t: Ukraine seeks €115 billion in foreign aid for 2027, Zelensky says
items.m: Ukraine will need €115 billion in external financing next year to sustain its economy and war effort against Russia, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, adding that Kyiv had secured commitments for about €90 billion from the European Union.

items.t: Ukraine says attack on Russian ships in Libya was self-defense
items.m: Both Russian naval vessels and cargo ships transporting military equipment were valid targets, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha says.

items.t: Zelenskyy says Ukraine sank Russian warship off Libya's coast
items.m: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country was behind attacks that sank a Russian warship and damaged a sanctioned cargo vessel off Libya.

items.t: Russian strike kills two people in Ukraine's Odesa region, governor says
items.m: Nov 24 - A Russian strike has killed two people and injured three more, including a child, in Ukraine's Black Sea region of Odesa, hitting cars and private and industrial buildings, Governor Oleh Kiper said on Telegram late on Tuesday.

items.t: China calls for normal flow of key livelihood supplies in Black Sea
items.m: A Chinese envoy on Monday called for ensuring the normal flow of essential supplies for people's livelihoods in the Black Sea, as the Ukraine crisis continues to drag on and hostilities keep escalating.

items.t: The Russian army’s secret death toll – podcast
items.m: Vladimir Putin has always kept the number of soldiers killed in Ukraine a secret, but at one point 720 were dying in 24 hours. Pjotr Sauer reports. Now documents leaked to the Guardian have revealed its true scale . The Guardian’s Russia affairs correspondent, Pjotr Sauer , tells Helen Pidd what reporters have discovered. items.t: Live: Two Libyan soldiers killed in Ukrainian attack on Russian vessels in Benghazi
items.m: Two Libyan soldiers have died from injuries sustained in an attack, claimed by Ukraine, on Russian ships near Benghazi, a senior figure in the administration in eastern Libya said late on Tuesday. Members of the European Parliament will convene in Strasbourg on Wednesday to discuss 'Europe’s role and capacity to protect the international order and secure a just and lasting peace for Ukraine.' items.t: Energy bills in Great Britain to rise 26% in January, lifting annual bills over £2,000
items.m: Ofgem’s price cap will increase for third quarter in a row after rise in wholesale cost of gas Millions of British households will face annual energy bills of more than £2,000 a year for the first time since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, as the cap on energy bills climbs for a third straight quarter. Gas and electricity prices will rise by 26% from January under the government’s new price cap after an increase in wholesale prices not experienced since the first winter after the invasion. items.t: North Korea Kicks Out Swiss Diplomats in Spat Linked to Ukraine War
items.m: The move followed Switzerland’s decision to impose sanctions on an international youth camp in North Korea, which is accused of hosting Ukrainian children for indoctrination.

items.t: Russian overnight strikes kill two in Odesa, set Kyiv apartment block ablaze
items.m: In an overnight assault, Russian forces targeted various regions in Ukraine, including Odesa and Kyiv. The attacks resulted in two fatalities and several injuries, with both civilians and children affected. Additionally, a drone strike in Kyiv sparked a significant fire in a high-rise building, causing two more injuries. Concurrently, a drone incident in Russia's Samara region led to serious consequences, including a death and power outages.

items.t: Trump administration shelves business deal proposals to persuade Russia to end Ukraine war: Report
items.m: This comes after the meeting between Trump, Putin and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, where the leaders discussed the Ukraine war.

items.t: Is Russia really aiming for a new European security architecture?

items.t: Zelensky says U.S. wants peace deal by January. Trump says he’s ‘not under a timeline’ for ending war.
items.m: U.S. President Donald Trump said he has no specific timeline for ending the Russia–Ukraine war. He was responding to comments from Volodymyr Zelensky, who said American negotiators are working to reach peace as soon as possible, ideally by January.

items.t: Lukashenko offers to fly Zelensky to Moscow for peace talks with Putin. ‘What am I, his suitcase?’ Zelensky responds.

items.t: French foreign minister defends Ukraine attacks on Russian ships in Libya
items.m: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Wednesday that Ukraine had been exercising its right to defend itself in weekend drone strikes against Russian ships in the waters around Benghazi in eastern Libya, an operation that stunned some of Kyiv's allies.

items.t: ‘Russia wants more than Ukraine,’ Germany’s Merz warns – Europe live
items.m: German chancellor, in wide-ranging speech, says Moscow is ‘escalating on a massive scale’ Meanwhile, Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Hungary’s Péter Magyar have hailed “a fresh start” in relations between their countries, resetting them after more than a decade of growing acrimony under Viktor Orbán. During his visit to Zakarpattia region – the first by a sitting Hungarian PM in 15 years – Magyar stressed his commitment to protecting the rights of some 60,000 ethnic Hungarians resident in the region. items.m: The administration of U.S. President Donald Trump has quietly abandoned the idea of using business deals with Russia as leverage to pressure the Kremlin into ending the war, Financial Times sources said. U.S. presidential envoy Steve Witkoff and Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, told European officials as much.
